front: Tu as passé un bon week-end ?
pronunciation: [tü ah pah-say an bohn wee-KEND]
back: Did you have a good weekend?
context: The Monday-morning question in every French office.

front: Oui, super ! Je suis allée voir mes parents.
pronunciation: [WEE, sü-PEHR ! zhuh swee zah-lay vwahr may pah-RAHN]
back: Yes, great! I went to see my parents.
context: 'Aller voir quelqu'un' = to go and see someone. Agreement: allée (a woman speaking).

front: Qu'est-ce que vous avez fait samedi ?
pronunciation: [kehs-kuh voo zah-vay feh sahm-DEE]
back: What did you do on Saturday?
context: Passé composé for completed weekend activities.

front: Samedi matin, j'ai fait la grasse matinée.
pronunciation: [sahm-dee mah-TAN, zhay feh lah gras mah-tee-NAY]
back: On Saturday morning I slept in.
context: 'Faire la grasse matinée' = to sleep in.

front: Ensuite, on a déjeuné en terrasse.
pronunciation: [ahn-SWEET, ohn nah day-zhuh-nay ahn teh-RAS]
back: Then we had lunch outside.

front: L'après-midi, nous nous sommes promenés au parc.
pronunciation: [lah-preh-mee-DEE, noo noo sum proh-muh-nay oh PARK]
back: In the afternoon, we went for a walk in the park.

front: Le soir, on est sortis avec des amis.
pronunciation: [luh SWAHR, ohn neh sor-TEE ah-vek day zah-MEE]
back: In the evening, we went out with friends.
context: With 'on' = nous, the participle often agrees: sortis.

front: On est rentrés vers deux heures du matin.
pronunciation: [ohn neh rahn-tray vehr duh zuhr dü mah-TAN]
back: We got home around 2 a.m.

front: Dimanche, je n'ai rien fait de spécial.
pronunciation: [dee-MAHNSH, zhuh neh ryan feh duh spay-SYAL]
back: On Sunday, I didn't do anything special.
context: 'Ne… rien' around the auxiliary: je n'ai rien fait. 'Rien de' + adjective.

front: Je me suis reposé toute la journée.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee ruh-poh-zay toot lah zhoor-NAY]
back: I rested all day.

front: J'ai regardé une série sur le canapé.
pronunciation: [zhay ruh-gar-day ün say-REE sür luh kah-nah-PAY]
back: I watched a series on the sofa.

front: Il faisait tellement beau qu'on a pique-niqué au bord de l'eau.
pronunciation: [eel fuh-zeh tel-mahn BOH kohn nah peek-nee-kay oh bor duh LOH]
back: The weather was so nice that we had a picnic by the water.

front: Je suis allé courir le long du canal.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zah-lay koo-reer luh lohn dü kah-NAL]
back: I went running along the canal.

front: On a fêté l'anniversaire de Léa.
pronunciation: [ohn nah feh-tay lah-nee-vehr-sehr duh lay-AH]
back: We celebrated Léa's birthday.

front: J'ai enfin rangé mon appartement.
pronunciation: [zhay ahn-fan rahn-zhay mohn nah-par-tuh-MAHN]
back: I finally tidied my apartment.
context: 'Ranger' = to tidy up. Adverbs like enfin go between auxiliary and participle.

front: Je suis allé au marché et j'ai cuisiné pour toute la semaine.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zah-lay oh mar-SHAY ay zhay kwee-zee-nay poor toot lah suh-MEN]
back: I went to the market and cooked for the whole week.

front: Le week-end est passé trop vite.
pronunciation: [luh wee-kend eh pah-say troh VEET]
back: The weekend went by too fast.

front: J'ai l'impression de ne pas m'être reposé.
pronunciation: [zhay lan-preh-syohn duh nuh pah meh-truh ruh-poh-ZAY]
back: I feel like I didn't rest at all.
context: Past infinitive: 'm'être reposé'. Negation before it: ne pas.

front: On a fait une petite escapade à la campagne.
pronunciation: [ohn nah feh tün puh-teet es-kah-PAD ah lah kahm-PAN-yuh]
back: We took a short trip to the countryside.

front: Il y avait des bouchons sur la route du retour.
pronunciation: [eel yah-veh day boo-SHOHN sür lah root dü ruh-TOOR]
back: There were traffic jams on the way back.

front: Je me suis couché tôt pour être en forme lundi.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee koo-shay TOH poor eh-trahn FORM lan-DEE]
back: I went to bed early to be fit for Monday.
context: 'Être en forme' = to be in good shape.

front: Rien de spécial, et toi ?
pronunciation: [ryan duh spay-SYAL, ay TWAH]
back: Nothing special, and you?
context: Typical reply to 'Tu as fait quoi ce week-end ?'

front: C'était un week-end très chargé.
pronunciation: [seh-teh tan wee-kend treh shar-ZHAY]
back: It was a very busy weekend.

front: Je n'ai pas vu le temps passer.
pronunciation: [zhuh neh pah vü luh tahn pah-SAY]
back: The time flew by.

front: Nous sommes allés au cinéma voir le dernier film de Jacques Audiard.
pronunciation: [noo sum zah-lay oh see-nay-MAH vwahr luh dehr-nyay feelm duh zhak oh-DYAR]
back: We went to the cinema to see Jacques Audiard's latest film.

front: Le film ne m'a pas plu.
pronunciation: [luh feelm nuh mah pah PLÜ]
back: I didn't like the film.
context: 'Plaire à' → ça m'a plu = I liked it.

front: Ça t'a plu, la soirée ?
pronunciation: [sah tah PLÜ, lah swah-RAY]
back: Did you enjoy the party?
context: Topic at the end: very natural spoken French.

front: J'ai rencontré quelqu'un de très sympa.
pronunciation: [zhay rahn-kohn-tray kel-kan duh treh san-PAH]
back: I met someone really nice.

front: On a fait la fête jusqu'au bout de la nuit.
pronunciation: [ohn nah feh lah FET zhüs-koh boo duh lah NWEE]
back: We partied all night long.

front: Le dimanche, c'est sacré : déjeuner en famille.
pronunciation: [luh dee-MAHNSH, seh sah-KRAY : day-zhuh-nay ahn fah-MEE]
back: Sundays are sacred: lunch with the family.
context: The long Sunday family lunch is a French institution.

front: Il a plu tout le week-end, alors on est restés à la maison.
pronunciation: [ee lah PLÜ tool wee-KEND, ah-lor ohn neh res-tay ah lah meh-ZOHN]
back: It rained all weekend, so we stayed home.
context: 'Il a plu' = passé composé of pleuvoir, for a closed period.

front: J'ai essayé un nouveau restaurant vietnamien.
pronunciation: [zhay eh-seh-yay an noo-voh res-toh-RAHN vyet-nah-MYAN]
back: I tried a new Vietnamese restaurant.

front: Vivement le week-end prochain !
pronunciation: [veev-MAHN luh wee-kend proh-SHAN]
back: Bring on next weekend!

front: Et toi, tu as fait quelque chose de sympa ?
pronunciation: [ay TWAH, tü ah feh kel-kuh shohz duh san-PAH]
back: And you, did you do anything nice?

front: Bon, on s'y remet : c'est lundi !
pronunciation: [BOHN, ohn see ruh-MEH : seh lan-DEE]
back: Right, back to work: it's Monday!
context: 'S'y remettre' = to get back to it.
